source_text: deprehendant daemones in concubitu coniugatos, et tamquam in sua operatione deprehensos, non sinant generare filios regeneratione liberandos Daemones instituisse connubium seminalem sexus utriusque mixtionem
pass_a_gloss: Deprehendant demon in concubitu coniugatos, and tamquam in his-own operatione deprehensos, not sinant generare sons regeneration liberandos demon instituisse connubium seminalem sex utriusque mixtionem.
pass_b_english: [They instituted] the union of seed between the two sexes.
Marital intercourse for the purpose of conceiving children is the devil’s work.
Demons would catch married people in intercourse and, finding them engaged in their own work, would not allow them to conceive children who were to be freed by rebirth.

choices.why: Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
